Burj Khalifa. The 828-meter supertall skyscraper completed in 2010 in Dubai, holding the record as the world's tallest building by architectural height since its completion. It was designed by American architect Adrian Smith with the Chicago firm Skidmore, Owings and Merrill, representing a synthesis of Western engineering and Middle Eastern urban ambition. The tower contains 163 floors above ground plus additional floors below, with a facade of reflective glass and anodized aluminum to minimize heat absorption in the desert climate. At 828 meters, this surpasses the Willis Tower's 442 meters, representing a technological leap enabled by advances in wind resistance and structural engineering. The building houses the At the Top observation deck at 124 stories, affording views across the Persian Gulf and the sprawling development of Dubai. It consumed approximately 330,000 tons of materials and required five years of construction, serving as both a luxury residence and commercial flagship for Dubai. The tower symbolizes the twenty-first-century shift of architectural ambition from Western cities to the Arabian Gulf and emerging global economies.
